requests.purpose: Carry one sealed customer-freight trailer through the corridor and toward a disclosed third-party facility, retaining the occupied cab.
requests.prompt: Use case illustration-story. Create a premium sculpted 2.5D editorial sprite atlas on genuine transparent alpha, no background. Subject a generic modern white long-haul tractor attached to a long enclosed pale grey box semitrailer, facing right in exact flat side elevation. Rounded aerodynamic cab, roof sensor pods, dark cab side window with simple seated safety-observer silhouette visibly in driver position, brushed alloy seams, ribbed trailer, black realistic tyres and hubs, muted deep petrol teal accent, warm copper glints. Coherent soft upper-left key and cool fill, tangible surfaces. Fully assembled truck occupies top two thirds, all wheels aligned to same horizontal ground contact. Bottom third has ONE separate matching black tyre and alloy hub in orthographic side view to enable wheel rotation. Large clean transparent gaps separate truck and tyre. No text, logos, trademarks, road, cargo, floor, shadows extending outside object, no extra views. Truck fully inside frame and silhouette readable at phone scale. This is disclosed generic transport illustration, not documentary evidence of actual Volvo equipment or driverless operation.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed generic illustration, not the actual Volvo truck, private software, cargo contents, operator, customer facility or observed route geometry. No driver removal, unloading method or measured performance is depicted.

requests.purpose: Contrast transfer-terminal and direct customer-facility endpoints and make the safety observer visibly present in the cab.
requests.prompt: Use case illustration-story. Create a matching premium sculpted 2.5D editorial support sprite atlas with genuine transparent alpha, no background or text. Exactly three separated props arranged left to right with large transparent gaps. Left a generic low industrial freight terminal front facade, concrete dock base and ribbed metal walls, two closed dock doors, worn maintained finish. Middle a different generic third-party customer freight facility facade with ONE prominent loading-bay opening and grounded dock sill, not a named real site. Right a close side-view cab window interior framing a seated safety-observer silhouette and clearly identifiable steering wheel, ordinary dark blue work shirt, no caricature facial detail, hands resting rather than acting. Match white grey petrol teal and muted copper palette, sculpted volumes, soft upper-left key and cool fill, tangible seams and material detail, consistent frontal perspective. Each object isolated entirely and large enough for native crop. No cargo contents, people unloading, safety numbers, private UI, words or brands. Disclosed generic facility and occupied-cab illustrations only, not actual sites or observed footage.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed generic illustration, not the actual Volvo truck, private software, cargo contents, operator, customer facility or observed route geometry. No driver removal, unloading method or measured performance is depicted.

clauses.text: On October fifth, Volvo and Waabi announced customer operations with Warp in Texas.
Their autonomous truck carries customer freight along the Dallas to Houston corridor, directly to third-party facilities.
Warp groups shipments from different customers.
It coordinates routes, capacity and timing.
An observer still sits in the driver's seat.
The companies plan to use these trips to prepare additional routes.
Customer freight reaches facilities with the observer aboard.
